_comment: Backlog row 665, second arc (API-QUEUE-V2-HIDES-TERMINAL-JOBS). The seam is bulk_downloader/app_queue.py: the fourth arm of the /api/queue/v2 classifier and the known/state pair on /api/queue/v2/job_log. Remote lane: BD_WORKER_MODE=mutate /home/mboyle/bd-worker-precut.sh <wt> <base> --spec tests/mutants/row665_absence_is_not_an_answer.json. EVERY ANCHOR HERE IS STRUCTURAL ON PURPOSE -- no quoted string, no literal, no '=' inside any matched span -- so that tests/test_row357_mutant_anchors_are_not_fragile.py can classify it without a producer record and without growing the capped stable-exception census; that is also why the seam names _UNKNOWN_STATE and lifts `state` out of the dict literal. M5 is the over-correction, because answering 'unknown' for EVERY job would also make every absent job unknown and would look like a pass to the four regression mutants alone. MA is the escape that refuted this cut's first generation (VERDICT: REFUTE, row665-B1-B-local): M2 alone (len(unclassified) -> 0) is caught for free by any test asserting a nonzero count, so it never exercised the cap-versus-count distinction the seam comment claims. MA reintroduces exactly that distinction and is caught only by the 201-seed test, which is why that test exists.
subject: absence from the v2 snapshot and from the per-job lookup is reported as an explicit state, never as silence

mutants.label: M1 the fourth arm is dead: an unrecognised status falls out of the payload again
M2 the bucket is reported but its count no longer counts
MA the count is capped along with its list, so an overflow hides behind the number
M3 the lookup drops the third value: an absent job reads as empty status again
M4 the lookup claims every url is known
M5 OVER-CORRECTION the lookup answers unknown for every job, present or not
